record.body: The dawn chorus is the burst of bird song that begins before sunrise and peaks in the first hours of daylight, when many species sing at once to defend territories and attract mates after the night. Singing at dawn is thought to help because sound carries well in the cool, still morning air, and because a male that sings vigorously after a night without food honestly advertises his condition. The chorus follows a sequence: different species start at different light levels, so the chorus builds species by species, and it fades as the day warms and feeding takes over. This record's primary layer is biophony, the birds themselves, while the still morning air is geophony at its quietest and any early traffic is anthrophony intruding on the chorus.
